newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty inches up vs basket, depos slip.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty inches up vs basket, depos slip.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed against the basket of currencies on Wednesday as banks cut foreign currency positions and foreign investors bought small amounts of Polish T-bills in secondary trade, dealers said.
They said that very often banks reduce foreign currency holdings on Wednesday to take advantage of the Friday value date and keep higher yielding zloty deposits over the weekend.
"Today's light selling trend was reinforced by foreign clients likely entering Polish treasuries," said Pawel Gajewski, forex dealer at Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 3.01/2.98 percent from the parity rate, stronger than Tuesday's 2.92/2.88 percent.
It was at 3.0675/85 to the dollar, up from 3.0685/95 on Tuesday and at 1.8350/55 to the mark, also up from 1.8385/95.
On the money market overnight rates fell to 22.45/22.70 percent from opening's 23.40/23.60 percent as funds rejected at today's NBP-bill tender flooded the market, dealers said.

They said the move signalled that 182-, 273-day NBP-bills would remain capped around 22.00 percent despite a recent rise in 91-day NBP-bill yields. Tomorrow/next fell to 22.45/22.75 percent from 23.40/23.65. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
